newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Merck sees strong 1997 profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Merck sees strong 1997 profit growth.

text.p: German drugs group Merck KGaA said Tuesday its 1996 profits surged 36 percent and said it expected further earnings growth, possibly in double digit percentage points, this year as well.

Describing 1996 as "an extremely successful year," Merck posted net profit of 502 million German marks ($297.6 million) for 1996 amid a 10.9 percent rise in sales to 6.95 billion marks ($4.1 billion).
Merck management board Chairman Hans Joachim Langmann later told a news conference that if sales registered double-digit growth in 1997, then profits would also grow in double-digits.
Langmann gave no dividend outlook for 1997, but said that Merck followed a "shareholder-friendly" route.

Merck's core pharmaceutical business fuelled the 1996 advance, with sales rising 16 percent. Laboratory sales rose 6.3 percent, while speciality chemicals sales advanced 5.1 percent. The German firm is not related to U.S. pharmaceutical company Merck & Co. Inc.
